adds.title: Keepin’ It “Real”: Israel’s Segregation of Transgender Prisoners and the Transgender/Cisgender Binary (Lihi Yona, Buffalo Journal of Gender, Law & Social Policy, Vol. 24, p. 43)
adds.summary: Law-journal article documenting that Israel’s response to transgender prisoners’ vulnerability has been to isolate/segragate them, keeping trans inmates apart from the rest of the prison population rather than placing them in facilities matching their gender identity. Establishes that a trans prisoner faces isolation-based custody as the default management practice.

adds.title: New Israel Fund – Victory for Transgender Rights in Israeli Prisons
adds.summary: October 2019 precedent-setting case: an Israeli court ordered the Israel Prison Service to provide hormone-replacement therapy to a trans woman prisoner and transfer her from a male prison to a female one, after ACRI petitioned. The prisoner was initially placed in a separate wing of the women’s prison, and ACRI prepared a further petition to have her housed with the general population — showing case-by-case placement review by the courts, and that trans women have at times been held in men’s prisons in Israel.

records.note: Israeli practice is case-by-case, court-reviewable placement. Documented pattern: trans prisoners managed by segregation/isolation (2015 law-journal analysis; a 2013 Supreme Court ruling cited regulations requiring transgender prisoners be kept apart from the general population). Trans women have been held in men’s prisons; a 2019 court order forced transfer of one trans woman from a men’s to a women’s prison (initially housed in a separate wing). 2023 news reported a court ordering gender-affirming care for a trans inmate. No blanket birth-sex placement rule is in force; individual assessment including “appearance” has been reported. Adds: 2 verified sources (fetched).

adds.title: Inside jails, gay men and trans women ‘wed’ fellow PDLs to escape abuse (Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism, by Aie Balagtas See)
adds.summary: Investigative feature on Manila City Jail: transgender women and gay men are held in the ordinary MALE dormitories (mandatory head-shaving on arrival for the male dorm), where they assume housekeeping/entertainer roles and informal same-sex “weddings” with male inmates are widely used by gangs as a survival/protection strategy against abuse. Documents that trans women in Philippine jails are housed by birth sex in male facilities with no gender-matched placement, and that safety comes from inmate hierarchies rather than policy.

adds.title: BJMP-Davao transfers LGBT inmates to annex facility for safety (SunStar Davao, by Ian Carl Espinosa)
adds.summary: Official practice documented: BJMP-Davao Community Relations chief Jail Senior Inspector Ellen Rose Saragena said LGBT detainees at Davao City Jail are relocated in batches to the City Jail Annex “to prevent abuse”, alongside persons with disabilities, the sick and senior citizens; three LGBT groupings live in the annex since its establishment. Shows the official Philippine response is administrative segregation of LGBT detainees into a separate annex for “safety”.

records.note: Philippines: trans prisoners are housed by birth sex in male facilities, with documented practice of separating LGBT detainees into dedicated annexes/dorms for “safety”. PCIJ (Dec 2022) documents trans women in Manila City Jail’s male dormitory, head-shaving on intake, and informal same-sex “weddings” used to escape abuse; SunStar (Mar 2023) reports BJMP-Davao relocating LGBT inmates in batches to the Davao City Jail Annex to prevent abuse. No statute mandates placement by gender identity; no national trans-inmate placement policy was found. Adds: 2 verified sources (fetched).
